sources.title: SciPy 1.14.1 least_squares documentation
sources.read_scope: Parameters, bounds, callable Jacobian, method-specific ftol/xtol/gtol and x_scale, max_nfev, returned status and Notes on LM and TRF. LM does not handle bounds and requires at least as many residual rows as variables; TRF supports bounds. MINPACK/STIR original papers were not read in this preparation.

sources.title: SciPy 1.14.1 BFGS documentation
sources.role: Maintained implementation companion, not independent analytic optimum
sources.read_scope: Options gtol, norm, c1/c2, hess_inv0 and precision-loss notes; no claim of reading a BFGS original paper.

sources.title: SciPy 1.14.1 L-BFGS-B documentation
sources.role: Separate software companion, with bounds=None; not identical to the original two-loop implementation
sources.read_scope: Options maxcor, ftol, gtol/projected-gradient convention, maxfun, maxiter and maxls.

sources.title: SciPy 1.14.1 line_search documentation
sources.read_scope: Signature, c1/c2, descent-direction requirement, returned failure None and evaluation counts. Cited textbook pages were not read.

sources.title: SciPy 1.14.1 curve_fit documentation
sources.role: Scope warning about sigma, absolute_sigma and locally linearized covariance
sources.read_scope: sigma/absolute_sigma and covariance interpretation sections. The penalized sandwich covariance in this study is derived independently; it is not presented as curve_fit output.

sources.title: On the limited memory BFGS method for large scale optimization
sources.year_role: bibliographic metadata retained from prior author-source record
sources.read_scope: Author-hosted PDF selected physical pages 3–5 (printed 2–4), rendered locally and visually inspected: limited storage, deletion of oldest correction, Eq. (2.1) inverse-BFGS, Algorithm 2.1 and Eq. (2.6) retained-update construction. No full-paper/proof/experiment or Section 4 scaling review. The selected original uses weak Wolfe; this study deliberately uses a separately specified strong-Wolfe line search. Current-gamma least-squares scaling is independently derived here, not attributed to unread text.

sources.title: Regularization Tools, Version 4.1 for Matlab 7.3
sources.read_scope: Official author manual: selected text around Section 2.5 and Section 2.9; physical pages 20 and 37 (printed 18 and 35) rendered locally and visually inspected. L-curve residual/solution norm tradeoff and discrepancy equation (2.61) were read. Four-point chord curvature here is a finite-list diagnostic, not the manual spline/corner algorithm, a theorem of optimal regularization or coverage. Original software (1994) and later article (2007) are separate bibliographic works and were not read.

sources.title: A new approach to variable metric algorithms
sources.read_scope: Prior saved publisher metadata/abstract-search record only. Original article full text remains unavailable/unread; no new request was made and no derivation is claimed to have been checked against it.

interpretation_notes: W is the declared optimization metric, not automatically inverse noise covariance. Sigma is specified separately.
The two-parameter spatially varying Bratu coefficient is the existing local educational extension, not an original-paper exact solution.
Fixed-gamma noise propagation is derived from local linearization of the estimator; it is not post-selection conditional covariance.
